title: The frame-purity lint fails a strip for a banned call named in a comment
body:
## Summary
lintStrip matches its clock/random/scheduler/CSS rules against the raw page, so a JS or CSS comment that names a banned construct fails the card and spends a fix round on the author's seat.

## Description
lib/foundry/strips/lint.ts:61-75 runs every RULES regex over the whole html with no comment stripping. pipeline/strips/CONTRACT.md:66 lists Math.random among the banned calls, so an author that writes `// never Math.random()` beside its PRNG is told it used Math.random. A lint-failed card goes to a fix turn (lib/foundry/strips/steps.ts lint -> producer plan), which is seat time, and the feedback names a violation the page does not have. Fixed: strip `//` and `/* */` comments inside <script> blocks and `/* */` inside <style> blocks (string-aware, so `"https://..."` survives for the network rule) and `<!-- -->` in markup before matching; the excerpt line numbers stay those of the original.

## Flow
- author writes `// deterministic: never Math.random(), never Date.now()` above a mulberry32 PRNG
- lint step -> lintStrip -> 2 findings (clock: Date.now, randomness: Math.random)
- card lint-failed, fix turn spent, feedback lists two calls the page never makes
- fix: comment-aware matcher; a real `return Math.random()` still fails

## Expected impact
5

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the lint fails only on code, not on prose about code
Before: probe (tsx over lintStrip): comment naming Math.random + Date.now -> 2 findings; CSS comment naming `transition: opacity 1s` -> 1 finding; a real `return Math.random()` -> 1 finding (correct). 3 of 3 comment cases flagged.
After: not built: predicted 0 of 3 comment cases flagged, the real call still flagged, `src="https://x"` still flagged
Method: probe - Before measured on lintStrip directly; After needs the stripper, and a gate weakened by a wrong stripper is a policy-loosen in disguise, so it goes to a worker with seeded violations (risk 5).
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/foundry/strips/lint.ts:61 `for (const r of RULES) { r.re.lastIndex = 0; ... while ((m = r.re.exec(html)))` - no comment stripping
probe: commentRandom ["clock: Date.now","randomness: Math.random (use a seeded PRNG)"]; cssComment ["time: running CSS transition"]; realRandom ["randomness: Math.random (use a seeded PRNG)"]
instrument: a vitest/probe case table over lintStrip: 3 comment-only pages (JS line, JS block, CSS block) expected clean; real Math.random, real `src="https://cdn"`, a `//` inside a string URL, and a `/*` inside a string expected flagged - seeded red on HEAD for the comment rows

title: A strip commit promotes a keep on a card that is no longer rendered
body:
## Summary
The verdict door takes a verdict only on a rendered card, but planStripCommit and commitStripRun honour any stored verdict, so a card that re-rendered as render-failed after its keep becomes a motion-style candidate.

## Description
lib/foundry/strips/store.ts:244 (cleanStripVerdicts) refuses a verdict unless JUDGEABLE.includes(card.status). planStripCommit (store.ts:296) and commitStripRun (store.ts:404) filter on the verdict alone. A strip job retried after triage marks the run running (steps.ts patch) and can leave a kept card `render-failed` or `lint-failed`; once the run is back at awaiting-triage the stale keep is committed: its html/style are copied into pipeline/foundry/motion-styles and a candidate row joins motion-styles.json; a stale reject deletes media of a card the operator never judged in that state. Fixed: plan and commit read a verdict only on a JUDGEABLE card (others count undecided), the Board's preview (lib/decision/v1/sources/strips.ts, same planStripCommit) follows for free.

## Flow
- operator keeps card a (rendered), rejects b
- job retried: a re-renders render-failed, b lint-failed; triage again
- planStripCommit -> kept 1 (styles [r--a]), rejected 1 (delete b's mp4+poster)
- fix: both read undecided; nothing promoted, nothing deleted

## Expected impact
5

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the commit applies the verdict door's own rule
Before: probe (tsx over planStripCommit): a render-failed card with keep + a lint-failed card with reject -> {kept:1, rejected:1, styles:["r--a"], delete:["b/strip.mp4","b/poster.jpg"]}
After: not built: predicted {kept:0, rejected:0, undecided:2, styles:[], delete:[]}
Method: probe - Before measured on the pure plan; the change also moves the Board's preview token and the Ledger's reading, two consumers outside this context, so it needs its own isolated gate run (M, risk 4).
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: foundry-strips.probe case: verdicts on two rendered cards, then flip their status in run.json to render-failed/lint-failed, assert preview counts undecided 2 and commit copies/deletes nothing; plus decision-v1-strips vitest for the preview

title: A Dojo improvement without pairs crashes the commit with a TypeError
body:
## Summary
blind.ts reads `imp.pairs ?? []` in five places, store.ts reads `imp.pairs` bare in four, so a cycle.json improvement with no pairs passes the gate and then throws inside commitCycle.

## Description
The loop sets improvements[0].pairs only after judging (pipeline/foundry/dojo_judge.py:223); a cycle that failed before judging is committable (store.ts commitCycle allows status failed). lib/foundry/training/blind.ts blindComplete/claimAllowed treat a missing pairs as zero pairs, so a reject verdict is accepted; lib/foundry/training/store.ts judgePickRate (`imp.pairs.length`), geminiAgreement, the cull loop (`for (const pair of imp.pairs)`) and findingsMarkdown then throw `Cannot read properties of undefined`. Whether the loop on the GPU machine ever writes an improvement without pairs is not visible from this checkout - the plan step that creates improvements lives there. Fixed: one `pairsOf(imp)` read used by every site, or a door that refuses the manifest with a 503 naming the field.

## Flow
- loop fails a cycle before judging: improvement has no pairs, status failed
- operator rejects the improvement on the Board (claimAllowed: 0 of 0 pairs picked = complete)
- commitCycle -> judgePickRate -> TypeError, a bare 500
- fix: pairsOf everywhere, the commit records 0 pairs

## Expected impact
3

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a commit of a pairless improvement lands or refuses by name
Before: simulation: 5 guarded reads (blind.ts) vs 4 bare (store.ts:219,227,368,256); a pairless reject reaches commit
After: not built: predicted commit lands with ledger row judge_pick_rate 0, pairs culled 0
Method: simulation - the premise (the loop writes a pairless improvement) depends on the GPU machine's plan step, not in this tree; the instrument is S.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/foundry/training/blind.ts:154 `(imp.pairs ?? []).filter(...)`; lib/foundry/training/store.ts:219 `if (!imp.pairs.length) return 0;`; store.ts cull `for (const pair of imp.pairs)`; pipeline/foundry/dojo_judge.py:223 `imp["pairs"] = pairs` (set only after judging)
instrument: foundry-training-store probe case: a failed cycle whose improvement omits pairs, reject verdict, commitCycle -> today TypeError, after: 1 ledger row

title: The Dojo store has no root override, so four probes write into foundry-out/training
body:
## Summary
lib/foundry/training/store.ts fixes OUT_ROOT at module load (outPath("training")), so foundry-training-store, foundry-dojo-blind, foundry-verdict-patch and foundry-commit-race all create their cycles in the operator's real foundry-out/training.

## Description
Strips has STRIPS_STORE_DIR (stripsRoot(), read per call) and its probe now uses it (1364abb1). The Dojo store has no equivalent: `const OUT_ROOT = outPath("training")` at lib/foundry/training/store.ts:79, so the four probes write `probe-*` cycles under <repo>/foundry-out/training, which the Library feed, the Ledger and the Board list while they live, and which a killed run leaves behind. Fixed: a `trainingRoot()` read per call honouring TRAINING_STORE_DIR (the strips shape), and the four probes pointed at a temp root with the same beforeEach assertion.

## Flow
- probe creates foundry-out/training/probe-commit-tmp-*
- a timeout under load kills it before afterEach
- the operator's Board lists a probe cycle
- fix: TRAINING_STORE_DIR temp root per test

## Expected impact
4

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the Dojo probes never touch the operator's store
Before: 4 probe files hard-code TRAINING_ROOT = <cwd>/foundry-out/training (foundry-training-store:25, foundry-dojo-blind:26, foundry-verdict-patch:53, foundry-commit-race:53)
After: not built: predicted 0 probe writes under foundry-out/training
Method: probe - counted by grep; the change spans a store seam plus four probe files (two shared with other contexts), so it is M and goes to a worker.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/foundry/training/store.ts:79 `const OUT_ROOT = outPath("training");`
tests/golden-path/foundry-training-store.probe.spec.ts:25 `const TRAINING_ROOT = path.join(process.cwd(), "foundry-out", "training");` (and 3 more files)
instrument: the beforeEach assertion from 1364abb1 applied to the four Dojo probes (store root outside <repo>/foundry-out), seeded red on HEAD

title: A refused anchored verdict write still leaves the improvement anchored
body:
## Summary
guardClaims writes anchored:true to blind.json before the verdict write it guards, so a PUT or a board-surface PATCH refused by the kernel (stale baseRev, unknown key) leaves the improvement anchored with no verdict.

## Description
lib/foundry/training/store.ts guardClaims (anchor=true path) calls patchBlind(..., anchored: true) and only then putTrainingVerdicts/patchTrainingVerdicts call the kernel, which can refuse with VerdictRevConflict 409. The blind phase for that improvement is then skipped for good: its ledger row will read basis anchored. In-tree callers today: the Board's apply uses surface "weir" (no anchoring) and putTrainingVerdicts has no production caller (tests only), so the path is reachable only through the API shape, not a screen. Fixed: anchor after the verdict write succeeds.

## Flow
- patchTrainingVerdicts(id, {set:{imp:'approve'}, baseRev: stale, surface:'board'})
- guardClaims -> patchBlind anchored:true written
- patchVerdictMap -> 409 stale base
- blind.json says anchored, verdicts.json unchanged

## Expected impact
2

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a refused write changes nothing
Before: walked: stale-rev board PATCH -> blind.json anchored:true, 409 returned
After: not built: predicted blind.json unchanged on 409
Method: simulation - walked through verdictLog.patchVerdictMap's rev check and guardClaims' order; the probe is S but the path has no production caller, so it was not worth this round's build.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/foundry/training/store.ts guardClaims: `if (!anchor) throw ...; await patchBlind(id, open.map((i) => ({ imp: i.id, anchored: true })));` then patchVerdictMap: `if (patch.baseRev !== current.rev) throw new VerdictRevConflict(current.rev);`
grep: putTrainingVerdicts only in tests/golden-path/foundry-verdict-patch.probe.spec.ts; lib/decision/v1/sources/dojo.ts:383 surface "weir"
instrument: foundry-dojo-blind probe case: stale-rev board PATCH, assert blind.json has no anchored entry after the 409

title: A strip's supporting image that failed leaves no word on its cards
body:
## Summary
steps.asset returns {ok:false, error} as an event when the image call throws, but writes nothing on the cards, so the card renders without its texture and run.json never says why.

## Description
lib/foundry/strips/steps.ts asset(): the catch returns `{ ok: false, approach, error }` and skips the patch that sets `c.asset`; the author turn then runs without inputs/assets/ (author.ts prepareTurn copies only an existing asset). The operator triaging a flat-looking strip sees no asset field and no error on the card; the reason lives only in the job's event stream. v1 behaved the same ("the strip renders without it"), which is a behaviour to keep, not a record to keep missing. Fixed: patch `c.assetError` (or `asset: { error }`) on the approach's cards.

## Flow
- approach declares leonardo: texture
- image call throws (provider down)
- asset step -> event ok:false; cards untouched
- card renders flat; triage shows no reason

## Expected impact
3

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a lost asset is recorded where the strip is judged
Before: walked: 0 of 1 failure paths in asset() write to run.json
After: not built: predicted 1 of 1
Method: simulation - the asset seam is fakeable (ImageMaker) but the field is a wire change to StripCard shared with pipeline/strips; left for a worker with the type and its readers in one write set.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/foundry/strips/steps.ts asset(): `} catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof Error)) throw e; return { ok: false, approach: approachId, error: e.message }; }` - no patch()
instrument: producer-strips vitest: an ImageMaker that throws, assert the approach's cards carry the error in run.json

title: The Dojo's chokepoint judge is not pinned on the pair or the ledger row
body:
## Summary
PairResult records gemini_model per pair but nothing names the chokepoint judge, so judge_agreement.chokepoint_vs_human in training-ledger.json cannot be compared across a judge change.

## Description
eval-harness golden path, 'The judge is inside the system under measurement' (technique judge-stability): the judge is pinned (model, version, rubric) and its drift measured. lib/foundry/training/types.ts PairResult carries `gemini_model` (the retry ladder can change it) but `judge_pick` has no model; TrainingLedgerRow.judge_agreement.chokepoint_vs_human (written by lib/foundry/training/store.ts blindFields) is therefore a trend over an unnamed instrument - a chokepoint swap on the GPU machine silently changes what the number means. Fixed: the loop writes `judge_model` per pair (or per cycle), the ledger row carries it beside the agreement.

## Flow
- loop changes its chokepoint model
- next cycle's chokepoint_vs_human drops
- nothing in the row says the judge changed

## Expected impact
5

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the judge-vs-human agreement names its judge
Before: 0 of 2 judge fields pinned for the chokepoint (pair: no model; ledger row: no model); gemini: 1 of 2 (pair only)
After: not built: both judges named on pair and row
Method: simulation - the writer is the loop on the GPU machine (cycle.json) and the ledger is the cross-machine channel: a contract with a consumer outside this checkout.
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
lib/foundry/training/types.ts PairResult: `judge_pick: ...; gemini_model?: string;` (no chokepoint model)
lib/foundry/training/store.ts blindFields: `judge_agreement: { chokepoint_vs_human: m.chokepoint_vs_human, ... }`

title: measureBlind's fallback seed differs from buildBlindMap's
body: measureBlind (lib/foundry/training/blind.ts) falls back to armInSlotA("", ...) when a pair is missing from the map, a different seed from the cycle id buildBlindMap uses. Rejected: every caller passes a map from withBlindMap, which fills every (improvement, pair) key from the real seed first; the fallback is unreachable.
evidence: lib/foundry/training/store.ts readBlind -> withBlindMap(id, cycle.improvements, stored); lib/decision/v1/sources/dojo.ts reads getCycle().blind (same)
